proposedDecisions.reason: A still-open decision that would directly affect how decisions.md is regenerated/re-exported once a repo edits it by hand.

proposedDecisions.statement: Confirming an inferred decision is often the first time that decision is written down. Exporting it (in decisions.md) belongs to the export-ownership feature, and the next scout will then find it as a recorded decision.

result.objective: A decisions.md file added to the session export bundle, written beside spec.md, listing each decision with its origin (user, interviewer, or repo recorded/inferred) and citation.
result.expectedOutcome: Exporting a session writes a decisions.md beside the spec in which every decision states its origin and, where it has one, its citation.
unknowns: Which decisions are included: only answered/settled ones, or also open, rejected or superseded ones, and repo decisions the user never confirmed?
What each entry looks like (heading, question, answer, rationale, origin label, citation format), and whether that shape must be parseable by the next scout as recorded decisions?
What citation a user- or interviewer-origin decision carries, given only repo-origin decisions currently store a citation?
Whether intent.md ships in the same feature or decisions.md is built alone despite the design note pairing them?
How decisions.md behaves on re-export and hand edits: plain manifest-owned overwrite/removal, or does it need the provenance/hash-guard concerns the scout spec deferred?

proposedDecisions.title: decisions.md only, or intent.md too
proposedDecisions.body: The design note pairs decisions.md with intent.md in a not-yet-built 'export ownership' feature, and the scout spec lists provenance in exported files and the manifest hash guard as sibling concerns. Does this feature build decisions.md alone, or take on its siblings too?

choices.label: decisions.md only
choices.rationale: Small and shippable, and it follows the existing planned-file pattern. The cost is that intent.md and the hash guard stay as separate, unbuilt features.

choices.label: decisions.md and intent.md together
choices.rationale: Delivers the pairing the design note describes in one go. It also doubles the interview surface, and intent.md's content has no settled shape yet.

choices.label: The whole export-ownership feature (decisions, intent, provenance, hash guard)
choices.rationale: Solves every related concern at once. It is a much bigger change that couples an easy renderer to the harder manifest-integrity work.

proposedDecisions.recommendedAnswer: decisions.md has a settled content shape and existing prior art (renderSpecFile, planExport). intent.md and the hash guard have neither, so bundling them makes the simple part wait on the unresolved parts.

proposedDecisions.title: Which tree decisions go into the file
proposedDecisions.body: A session's tree holds decisions in several states: settled, open or unasked, blocked, stale, and ones answered unknown, deferred or prototype-flagged. It also holds repo decisions the user dropped. Which of these does decisions.md record?

choices.label: Settled decisions only
choices.rationale: The file stays a clean record of what was decided, and the next scout can safely treat every entry as a recorded decision. Open questions do not appear in it at all.

choices.label: Settled decisions, plus an 'Unresolved' section for open, deferred and unknown ones
choices.rationale: Keeps loose ends visible to a reader. The risk is that a later scout reads an unresolved item as a recorded decision unless the section is clearly marked and the scout skips it.

choices.label: Every decision in the tree, each with its state
choices.rationale: A full audit trail. It is noisy, and most entries would not be decisions at all, which undermines the file's use as scout input.

proposedDecisions.recommendedAnswer: The recorded loop means whatever lands in decisions.md comes back on the next scout run as a 'recorded' decision. Anything unsettled that gets into the file would be read as a constraint that was never agreed. Loose ends already belong in the spec and the handoff.

proposedDecisions.title: What 'origin' means per entry
proposedDecisions.body: introducedBy records who proposed the question (interviewer, user or repo). It does not record who authored the answer: the user may have accepted the interviewer's recommendation in one click or written their own answer. Which one does the origin label report?

choices.label: Who introduced the decision (introducedBy as stored)
choices.rationale: Needs no new data and maps straight onto the stored enum. It loses the difference between 'the interviewer proposed it and the user rubber-stamped it' and 'the user overrode the recommendation'.

choices.label: Introducer plus how the answer was reached (accepted recommendation, picked another choice, or wrote their own)
choices.rationale: A reader can tell a rubber stamp from a deliberate choice, which is the provenance people actually want. It only works if the answer kind is stored or can be derived, and that may need new data.

choices.label: Who authored the answer only
choices.rationale: Focuses on accountability for the outcome. It drops the stored origin enum, which contradicts the settled content shape.

proposedDecisions.recommendedAnswer: Origin is only useful if it tells a later reader how much weight a decision carries. An accepted default and a deliberate override from the user carry different weight, and introducedBy alone cannot tell them apart. If answer kind turns out not to be derivable, fall back to the first choice.

proposedDecisions.title: What 'citation' means for user and interviewer decisions
proposedDecisions.body: Repo decisions already carry a file:line citation. Decisions introduced by the user or the interviewer have no file to point at. What goes in their citation slot?

choices.label: Session reference: session title or id plus the round it was settled in
choices.rationale: Every entry gets a citation that can be traced back to the Grill Room session. It relies on sessions staying retrievable, and a reader outside the app cannot follow it.

choices.label: The spec.md section the decision shaped
choices.rationale: Points to an artifact in the same bundle, so it can be followed inside the repo. Not every decision maps cleanly onto one spec section, and the mapping is not tracked today.

choices.label: No citation; only repo decisions are cited
choices.rationale: Simplest option, and it never invents provenance. Most entries would have an empty citation, which only partly meets 'each with its citation'.

proposedDecisions.recommendedAnswer: A session-and-round reference is always available, is honest, and fills every entry's citation slot. A spec-section mapping would mean new tracking that nothing does today.

proposedDecisions.title: Re-exporting repo decisions that were kept unchanged
proposedDecisions.body: A repo decision the user kept is already recorded at its source (for example docs/design/sdlc-artifact-chain.md:91). If decisions.md restates it, the next scout finds the same decision twice: once at the original and once in decisions.md, which cites the original. How are kept repo decisions handled?

choices.label: Include them, citing the original source, and mark them as carried from the repo
choices.rationale: decisions.md becomes the complete decision set for this feature. The next scout sees duplicates and has to dedupe by citation or key.

choices.label: Include only repo decisions the interview reopened; list kept ones as references (key + citation, with no restated statement)
choices.rationale: Restates only what this session changed, so there is nothing for the scout to double-count. The file on its own is no longer a full picture.

choices.label: Omit kept repo decisions entirely
choices.rationale: No duplication at all. A reader loses the constraints this feature was built under.

proposedDecisions.recommendedAnswer: The recorded loop turns anything restated into a second recorded source, so restating unchanged decisions breeds duplicates on every export. Keeping kept decisions as bare references preserves the context without making a second copy. Reopened decisions are the ones this session actually owns.

proposedDecisions.title: What each entry says beyond origin and citation
proposedDecisions.body: Besides origin and citation, what does each decision entry carry?

choices.label: Title, the answer, and the reasoning behind it
choices.rationale: A lean statement of the current truth that a scout can parse easily. The alternatives that were weighed are lost.

choices.label: Title, question, answer, reasoning, and the rejected choices with their rationale (ADR-style)
choices.rationale: A full decision record: a reader can see what was traded away. Entries get long, and the rejected options could be misread as live options.

choices.label: Title and answer only
choices.rationale: The most compact option. It drops the reasoning, which is what makes a decision record worth keeping.

proposedDecisions.recommendedAnswer: The file feeds the next scout and states the current truth. Reasoning is what lets a later reader reopen a decision on purpose. Rejected alternatives can stay in the session and do not need to be in the repo.

proposedDecisions.title: Markdown layout of an entry
proposedDecisions.body: How is each entry laid out, so that people can read it and the next scout can reliably pick it up as a recorded decision: a heading per decision keyed by the stable decision key, the fields as a labelled list, and dependsOn rendered as links to other entries' anchors?

choices.label: One heading per decision (stable key as anchor), labelled field list, dependsOn as anchor links
choices.rationale: Stable, linkable and easy to cite at file:line. It is more verbose than a table.

choices.label: A single table, one row per decision
choices.rationale: Compact and easy to scan. Long reasoning breaks tables, and citing a row is awkward.

proposedDecisions.recommendedAnswer: The file must be citable by a later scout, and a heading per key gives each decision its own stable line to point at.

proposedDecisions.title: Wording and source of the 'how it was answered' label
proposedDecisions.body: You chose to show the introducer together with how the answer was reached. The answer kinds this session uses are accepted-recommendation, own-answer and repo-established; picking a non-recommended choice is presumably a kind of its own. I cannot check whether each settled decision persists its answer kind, so please confirm. This decision also fixes the wording the file prints, for example 'interviewer · accepted recommendation', 'interviewer · user's own answer', 'user', 'repo (recorded) · kept'.

choices.label: Print the stored answer kind verbatim, mapped to plain phrases (accepted recommendation / chose another option / own answer)
choices.rationale: Reuses data that already exists and needs no new tracking. It depends on the answer kind being persisted with every settled decision.

choices.label: Add answer-kind persistence first, then print it
choices.rationale: Needed if the kind is only transient today. Adds a store change to a feature that was meant to be a renderer only.

choices.label: Fall back to introducedBy only
choices.rationale: No data risk at all. It gives up the distinction you just chose to keep.

proposedDecisions.recommendedAnswer: The session state already tells accepted-recommendation apart from own-answer, which suggests the kind is stored. Map it to plain phrases so the file reads as prose, not enum values. Take the second option only if the build finds the kind is not persisted.

proposedDecisions.title: How a reopened repo decision appears
proposedDecisions.body: A repo decision the user reopened and answered differently now contradicts its original source (for example a design note). decisions.md restates it, and the next scout will find both the stale original and the new entry. How does the entry present the change?

choices.label: New answer and reasoning, origin 'repo (recorded/inferred) · reopened', citation to the original, plus a 'Supersedes' line quoting the original statement
choices.rationale: A later scout or reader can see which source is stale and why. The entry is a little longer.

choices.label: New answer only, citing the original with no mention of what changed
choices.rationale: Lean. A scout finds two contradicting 'recorded' statements and has no signal about which one wins.

choices.label: Also edit or flag the original source document
choices.rationale: Removes the contradiction at its root. It writes outside the bundle, which the manifest's removal-only ownership does not cover, and it is out of scope.

proposedDecisions.recommendedAnswer: The recorded loop means both statements come back as recorded decisions. An explicit 'Supersedes' line is the only in-bundle way to tell the next scout which one wins, and it does not touch files the export does not own.

proposedDecisions.title: When decisions.md is written at all
proposedDecisions.body: Some sessions will have no settled user or interviewer decisions and no reopened repo decisions, only kept repo references (or nothing at all). Is decisions.md still planned?

choices.label: Plan it only when there is at least one full entry; otherwise leave it out of the plan
choices.rationale: No near-empty files. On a re-export, the manifest removes a decisions.md that an earlier export wrote. The cost is that the file's presence varies between exports.

choices.label: Always plan it, even if it holds only references or an empty-state line
choices.rationale: Predictable bundle shape. A near-empty file gets committed, and the next scout reads it.

proposedDecisions.recommendedAnswer: The manifest already handles files that drop out of the plan, so leaving it out is safe. A reference-only file adds nothing the original sources do not already say.

proposedDecisions.title: Order of entries
proposedDecisions.body: In what order do entries appear in the file?

choices.label: Tree order: prerequisites before the decisions that depend on them, ties broken by settle order
choices.rationale: Reads as the design unfolds and keeps dependsOn links pointing upward. It needs a topological sort in the renderer.

choices.label: Settle order (round by round)
choices.rationale: Trivial to render, and it mirrors the interview. It exposes the editing process rather than the design, and re-exports can shuffle entries.

choices.label: Grouped by origin (repo, user, interviewer)
choices.rationale: Makes provenance easy to scan. It splits related decisions apart.

proposedDecisions.recommendedAnswer: The file should state the current design, not how the interview went. Tree order is stable across re-exports, which keeps diffs and line citations stable too.

proposedDecisions.title: Where the renderer lives and how it is tested
proposedDecisions.body: You dropped the repo constraint that export content is decided by pure, filesystem-free functions in export.ts, so this feature may depart from it. Does the decisions.md renderer follow that boundary anyway?

choices.label: Pure renderDecisionsFile in export.ts, wired into planExport, unit-tested there and covered through preview-export/export-session
choices.rationale: Matches renderSpecFile and renderTicketFile, and makes the renderer easy to test as input → string. There is nothing new to learn.

choices.label: Render inside export-bundle.ts, next to the writes
choices.rationale: One fewer hop. It mixes content decisions with filesystem code, unlike every other exported file.

proposedDecisions.recommendedAnswer: Dropping the constraint gave you freedom, but no reason to use it here. Following the existing boundary costs nothing, and the bundle planner then picks up the file for free.

done.summary:
Every branch of the tree is settled.

**Scope and placement**
- decisions.md is exported beside spec.md, the tickets, HANDOFF.md and the briefs (repo, recorded).
- This feature builds decisions.md only. intent.md, provenance in exported files and the manifest hash guard remain separate, unbuilt features.

**What goes in**
- Only settled decisions. Open, blocked, stale, unknown, deferred and prototype-flagged decisions are left out, and so are repo decisions the user dropped. Loose ends belong in the spec and the handoff.
- Kept repo decisions appear only as bare references (key + citation), never restated, so the next scout does not find them twice.
- Reopened repo decisions get a full entry: the new answer and its reasoning, origin 'repo (recorded/inferred) · reopened', a citation to the original source, and a 'Supersedes' line quoting the original statement. The original source file is not touched.
- decisions.md is planned only when there is at least one full entry. Otherwise it drops out of the plan, and the manifest removes any copy an earlier export wrote.

**Entry content**
- Each entry carries its origin, citation, title, answer and the reasoning behind the answer. Rejected alternatives stay in the session.
- Origin combines introducedBy (interviewer, user or repo, plus recorded/inferred for repo) with how the answer was reached, taken from the stored answer kind and printed as plain phrases (accepted recommendation / chose another option / own answer). If the build finds the answer kind is not persisted, persist it first; if that is not possible, fall back to introducedBy alone.
- Citation is present only for repo-origin entries. For user and interviewer entries the field is null.

**Layout and order**
- One heading per decision, anchored by its stable key, with the fields as a labelled list and dependsOn rendered as anchor links.
- Entries appear in tree order (prerequisites first, ties broken by settle order), so re-exports keep diffs and line citations stable.

**Implementation**
- A pure renderDecisionsFile in export.ts, wired into planExport next to renderSpecFile and renderTicketFile, unit-tested there and covered through preview-export and export-session. The bundle planner, preview, write and manifest pick it up as a new planned file with no special handling.

reviews.reason: The layout still applies to every full entry, and those are still settled decisions only. Your new answer lists Unresolved loose ends by title, so they appear as a plain list under their own section heading. They get no per-key headings or anchors, and a scout cannot mistake them for citable recorded entries. The heading-per-key layout is exactly what keeps the two kinds visibly apart.

The Unresolved section creates a case the old answer never considered: a session with no full entries but some open, deferred, unknown or prototype-flagged loose ends. The old rule, 'plan it only when there is at least one full entry', would silently drop those loose ends from decisions.md.
reviews.title: When decisions.md is written at all, now that it has an Unresolved section
reviews.body: decisions.md now has two parts: full entries (settled decisions, including reopened repo decisions) and an Unresolved section listing loose ends by title. Kept repo decisions appear only as bare references. What makes the file worth planning?

choices.label: Plan it only when there is at least one full entry; Unresolved items or references alone do not trigger it
choices.rationale: decisions.md stays a file of decisions, and the next scout never finds one with nothing recorded in it. A session with only loose ends shows them in spec.md and HANDOFF.md only.

choices.label: Plan it when there is at least one full entry or at least one Unresolved item
choices.rationale: Loose ends are always visible in decisions.md, as your new answer intends. The cost is that some exports write a decisions.md with no decisions at all, which the next scout still reads as a decisions file.

choices.label: Always plan it
choices.rationale: Predictable bundle shape. It commits near-empty or reference-only files that add nothing the original sources do not already say.

reviews.recommendedAnswer: The Unresolved section exists to put loose ends next to the decisions they sit beside. With no decisions, it only repeats what spec.md and HANDOFF.md already carry, and a decisions file with no decisions is a confusing input for the next scout. The manifest still removes an earlier decisions.md that drops out of the plan.

reviews.reason: Full entries are still settled decisions, and tree order still gives them stable diffs and line citations. The Unresolved section is clearly separated, so it follows all full entries and can list its titles in the same tree order. Nothing in the new answer calls for regrouping or reordering the entries.

proposedDecisions.title: How the next scout is kept from reading Unresolved items as decisions
proposedDecisions.body: The Unresolved section only works if the next scout skips it. A human sees a heading, but the scout reads the whole file as a recorded source. What stops it from lifting an Unresolved title as a recorded decision?

choices.label: Markup only: a fixed '## Unresolved (not decisions)' heading, plain list items with no key anchors, and a one-line note saying these are open questions
choices.rationale: Stays inside this feature, with no scout change. It relies on the scout's model honouring the wording, which is a soft guarantee.

choices.label: Markup plus a scout rule: the scout's prompt or parser explicitly ignores the Unresolved section of any decisions.md
choices.rationale: A hard guarantee that the loop cannot turn a loose end into a constraint. It touches project-scout code, a separate feature, which widens the scope you kept to decisions.md only.

choices.label: Let the scout pick them up, but as open questions rather than recorded decisions
choices.rationale: Loose ends carry over to the next session as questions to ask, which may be the most useful outcome. It needs a new 'open question' category in the scout, a larger change.

proposedDecisions.recommendedAnswer: decisions-md-scope keeps this feature to the renderer. Clear markup (a heading that says 'not decisions', and no key anchors, so there is nothing citable) is the strongest guard this feature can ship alone. A scout-side rule or carrying loose ends forward is worth a follow-up ticket, not a scope expansion now.

proposedDecisions.title: Exactly which states land in Unresolved, and what each line shows
proposedDecisions.body: Your answer names open, deferred, unknown and prototype-flagged. The tree also has blocked decisions (waiting on a prerequisite), stale ones (downstream of a reopened answer) and dropped repo decisions. Which states belong in the list, and does each line show its state next to the title?

choices.label: Every non-settled decision except dropped repo decisions (open, unasked, blocked, stale, deferred, unknown, prototype-flagged), each as 'title — state'
choices.rationale: Nothing unsettled is silently missing, and the state tells a reader why each item is open. Blocked items can make the list longer.

choices.label: Only the four states you named, title only
choices.rationale: Matches your wording exactly, and the list stays short. Blocked and stale items vanish from the file, even though they are just as undecided.

choices.label: Every non-settled decision, dropped repo decisions included, each with its state
choices.rationale: The fullest picture. Dropped repo decisions are not open questions; the user deliberately set them aside, so listing them as unresolved misstates them.

proposedDecisions.recommendedAnswer: 'Every loose end' should mean every loose end: a blocked or stale decision is as undecided as a deferred one. The state label costs one word per line and tells a reader whether an item needs an answer or is waiting on another decision. Dropped repo decisions were a choice, not a loose end.

done.summary:
Every branch of the tree is settled.

**Scope and placement**
- decisions.md is exported beside spec.md, the tickets, HANDOFF.md and the briefs (repo, recorded).
- This feature builds decisions.md only. intent.md, provenance in exported files, the manifest hash guard and any change to the scout remain separate work. A scout-side rule that skips the Unresolved section, or carries loose ends forward as open questions, is a candidate follow-up ticket.

**What goes in**
- Full entries are for settled decisions only.
- Kept repo decisions appear only as bare references (key + citation), never restated, so the next scout does not find them twice.
- Reopened repo decisions get a full entry: the new answer and its reasoning, origin 'repo (recorded/inferred) · reopened', a citation to the original source, and a 'Supersedes' line quoting the original statement. The original source file is not touched.
- A clearly separated Unresolved section lists every other non-settled decision (open, unasked, blocked, stale, deferred, unknown, prototype-flagged) as 'title — state'. Dropped repo decisions are left out; they were a choice, not a loose end.
- The Unresolved section is guarded by markup alone: a fixed '## Unresolved (not decisions)' heading, a one-line note that these are open questions, and plain list items with no key anchors, so nothing in it can be cited.
- decisions.md is planned only when there is at least one full entry. Unresolved items or references alone do not trigger it. When it drops out of the plan, the manifest removes a copy an earlier export wrote.

**Entry content**
- Each full entry carries its origin, citation, title, answer and the reasoning behind the answer. Rejected alternatives stay in the session.
- Origin combines introducedBy (interviewer, user or repo, plus recorded/inferred for repo) with how the answer was reached, taken from the stored answer kind and printed as plain phrases (accepted recommendation / chose another option / own answer). If the build finds the answer kind is not persisted, persist it first; if that is not possible, fall back to introducedBy alone.
- Citation is present only for repo-origin entries. For user and interviewer entries the field is null.

**Layout and order**
- One heading per full entry, anchored by its stable key, with the fields as a labelled list and dependsOn rendered as anchor links.
- Full entries appear in tree order (prerequisites first, ties broken by settle order), which keeps diffs and line citations stable. The Unresolved section comes after all full entries, in the same tree order.

**Implementation**
- A pure renderDecisionsFile in export.ts, wired into planExport next to renderSpecFile and renderTicketFile, unit-tested there and covered through preview-export and export-session. The bundle planner, preview, write and manifest pick it up as a new planned file with no special handling.

result.markdown:
## Problem Statement

A Grill Room interview produces a design tree of decisions, each with an origin (the interviewer, the user, or the repo) and, for repo decisions, a recorded or inferred source with a citation. Only part of that reaches the repository. The export bundle writes a spec, tickets, a handoff and briefs, but never a record of the decisions themselves.

This causes three problems for someone who has finished a session and exported it:

- **The decisions stay inside the app.** A teammate or a later reader cannot see what was decided, who proposed it, or whether the user deliberately chose an answer or just accepted a default.
- **The next scout has nothing to read.** A scout run on the same project cannot pick up the session's decisions as recorded decisions, so the loop the design intends (export, commit, scout again) is broken.
- **Changes to repo decisions are invisible.** When the interview reopens a repo decision and answers it differently, nothing in the repo says the original source is now superseded. A later scout would find only the stale statement.
- **Loose ends vanish from the decision record.** Open, deferred, blocked or stale questions are not visible next to the decisions they sit beside.

## Solution

Exporting a session writes a `decisions.md` beside `spec.md`, the tickets, `HANDOFF.md` and the briefs.

The file contains:

- **One entry per settled decision.** Each entry has a stable heading anchored by the decision's key and a labelled field list: title, answer, the reasoning behind the answer, origin and citation. Dependencies are rendered as links to the other entries' anchors.
- **Origin that says who introduced the decision and how it was answered.** For example "interviewer · accepted recommendation", "interviewer · own answer", "user", or "repo (recorded) · reopened".
- **Citations only where there is a real source.** Repo-origin entries cite their original file and line. User and interviewer entries have no citation.
- **Reopened repo decisions as full entries with a "Supersedes" line** quoting the original statement, so a reader or a later scout can tell the original source is stale.
- **Kept repo decisions as bare references** (key and citation only), so the same decision is never restated in a second place.
- **A clearly separated Unresolved section, placed after all entries.** It lists every non-settled decision as "title — state" under a heading marked "not decisions", with a one-line note, and no anchors. Dropped repo decisions are not listed.

The file is only produced when there is at least one full entry. It goes through the same export plan, preview, write and manifest as every other exported file, so a re-export that no longer produces it removes the old copy.

## User Stories

1. As a session owner, I want exporting a session to also write a decisions.md beside the spec, so that the decisions I made reach the repository together with the spec.
2. As a session owner, I want decisions.md to appear in the export preview like the other planned files, so that I can see it before anything is written.
3. As a session owner, I want decisions.md listed in the export manifest, so that later re-exports own and manage it the same way as the spec and the tickets.
4. As a session owner, I want a re-export to remove a decisions.md that an earlier export wrote once the new plan no longer includes it, so that a stale decision record never lingers.
5. As a session owner, I want no decisions.md produced when the session has no settled decisions of its own, so that the repo does not collect empty or reference-only decision files.
6. As a session owner, I want a session with only loose ends to leave its loose ends in the spec and the handoff, not in a decisions file with no decisions, so that every decisions.md actually contains decisions.
7. As a reader of the repo, I want every settled decision from the session to appear as its own entry, so that I can see the full set of choices behind the feature.
8. As a reader, I want each entry to show the decision's title, so that I can scan the file quickly.
9. As a reader, I want each entry to show the answer, so that I know what was decided.
10. As a reader, I want each entry to show the reasoning behind the answer, so that I understand why it was decided and can reopen it on purpose.
11. As a reader, I want rejected alternatives left out of the file, so that nobody mistakes a rejected option for a live one.
12. As a reader, I want each entry to show who introduced the decision (interviewer, user or repo), so that I know where the question came from.
13. As a reader, I want each entry to show how the answer was reached (accepted recommendation, chose another option, or own answer), so that I can tell a one-click default from a deliberate choice.
14. As a reader, I want the origin written as plain phrases rather than internal enum values, so that the file reads naturally.
15. As a reader, I want repo-origin entries to say whether the repo source was recorded or inferred, so that I know how firm the original statement was.
16. As a reader, I want repo-origin entries to carry the original file-and-line citation, so that I can go straight to the source.
17. As a reader, I want user and interviewer entries to have no citation, so that the file never invents provenance that does not exist.
18. As a reader, I want each entry under its own heading anchored by its stable decision key, so that I can link to a specific decision.
19. As a reader, I want an entry's dependencies rendered as links to the entries they depend on, so that I can follow the design tree inside the file.
20. As a reader, I want entries ordered so that prerequisites come before the decisions that depend on them, so that the file reads as the design unfolds.
21. As a reader, I want ties in that order broken by the order in which decisions were settled, so that the order is deterministic.
22. As a reviewer of a pull request, I want the entry order to stay stable across re-exports, so that diffs show real changes and not reshuffling.
23. As a later scout or reader, I want line citations into decisions.md to stay stable across re-exports, so that references to it keep pointing at the right decision.
24. As a reader, I want a repo decision that the interview reopened to appear as a full entry, so that the new answer and its reasoning are recorded.
25. As a reader, I want a reopened repo decision's origin to say "repo (recorded/inferred) · reopened", so that I can see it was deliberately changed.
26. As a reader, I want a reopened repo decision to cite its original source, so that I can find the statement it replaces.
27. As a reader, I want a reopened repo decision to carry a "Supersedes" line quoting the original statement, so that I know which of the two sources wins.
28. As a maintainer, I want the export never to edit or flag the original source of a reopened decision, so that the export only touches files it owns.
29. As a reader, I want repo decisions kept unchanged listed as bare references (key and citation), so that I can see the constraints the feature was built under.
30. As a later scout, I want kept repo decisions never restated in decisions.md, so that I do not find the same decision twice.
31. As a reader, I want dropped repo decisions left out entirely, so that deliberately set-aside constraints are not presented as decisions or as loose ends.
32. As a reader, I want an Unresolved section after all full entries, so that I can see what the session left open next to what it decided.
33. As a reader, I want the Unresolved section to list every non-settled decision (open, unasked, blocked, stale, deferred, unknown and prototype-flagged), so that no loose end is silently missing.
34. As a reader, I want each Unresolved line to show the decision's state next to its title, so that I know whether it needs an answer or is waiting on another decision.
35. As a reader, I want Unresolved items listed in the same tree order as the entries, so that they read alongside the related decisions.
36. As a later scout, I want the Unresolved section headed "Unresolved (not decisions)" with a one-line note that these are open questions, so that I do not read them as recorded decisions.
37. As a later scout, I want Unresolved items to be plain list items with no key anchors, so that nothing in that section can be cited as a decision.
38. As a later scout, I want decisions.md in the repo to be readable as a recorded source, so that the next session on the project starts from these decisions.
39. As a developer, I want the decisions.md content rendered by a pure function that takes the session's decision data and returns the file text, so that it can be tested without a filesystem.
40. As a developer, I want that renderer to sit next to the existing spec and ticket renderers and be wired into the export plan, so that the bundle planner, preview, write and manifest pick it up with no special handling.
41. As a developer, I want the renderer to use the decision data the tree already resolves (origin, repo source, citation, original statement, answer, answer kind), so that no new data is added unless it is actually missing.
42. As a developer, I want the answer kind persisted with every settled decision, so that the "how it was answered" label is always available.
43. As a developer, I want a documented fallback to printing only the introducer if the answer kind cannot be persisted or derived, so that the export never blocks on it.
44. As a team member reading the repo later, I want decisions.md to state the current design and not the history of the interview, so that the file stays a clean source of truth.

## Implementation Decisions

- **Scope.** This feature builds decisions.md only. intent.md, provenance in the other exported files, the manifest hash guard and any change to the scout are separate work.
- **Placement.** decisions.md is written at the bundle root, beside the spec, tickets, handoff and briefs. This follows the recorded design decision.
- **Module boundary.** A pure decisions renderer is added to the export rendering module, alongside the existing spec and ticket renderers.
  - It takes the session's resolved decision tree and returns markdown text.
  - It has no filesystem access.
  - The export planning step calls it and adds decisions.md to the planned files.
  - The bundle layer's preview, write, manifest and removal logic handle it generically, like every other planned file.
  - This matches the existing pure/filesystem split. That constraint was dropped as a binding rule for this session, but the feature follows it anyway.
- **Planning rule.** decisions.md is planned only when there is at least one full entry, meaning a settled decision that is not a kept repo decision.
  - Unresolved items alone do not trigger it.
  - Kept-repo references alone do not trigger it.
  - When it is not planned, the existing manifest behaviour removes a copy an earlier export wrote.
- **Inclusion rules.**
  - A full entry is written for each settled decision whose origin is interviewer or user, and for each repo decision the interview reopened.
  - Kept repo decisions appear only as bare references: key and citation, with no restated statement.
  - Dropped repo decisions do not appear.
  - Every other non-settled decision appears in the Unresolved section. That covers open, unasked, blocked, stale, deferred, unknown and prototype-flagged.
- **Entry content.** Each full entry has its title, answer, reasoning, origin and citation. The question text and rejected choices are not exported.
- **Origin label.** The label combines the stored introducer (interviewer, user or repo, plus recorded or inferred for repo) with how the answer was reached.
  - How the answer was reached comes from the stored answer kind, mapped to plain phrases: "accepted recommendation", "chose another option", "own answer".
  - A reopened repo decision is labelled "repo (recorded/inferred) · reopened".
  - If the build finds the answer kind is not persisted, it is persisted first.
  - If that is not feasible, the label falls back to the introducer alone.
- **Citation.** Repo-origin entries and references carry their original file-and-line citation. User and interviewer entries have a null citation, and no session reference is made up for them.
- **Reopened repo decisions.** Each one has the new answer and reasoning, the reopened origin label, a citation to the original source, and a "Supersedes" line quoting the original repo statement. The original source file is never modified.
- **Layout.**
  - Each full entry is a heading anchored by its stable decision key, followed by a labelled field list.
  - Dependencies are rendered as links to the anchors of the other entries.
  - The Unresolved section comes after all full entries. It has a fixed heading, "Unresolved (not decisions)", and a one-line note saying these are open questions and not decisions.
  - Each Unresolved item is a plain list item, "title — state", with no anchor.
- **Ordering.** Full entries are topologically sorted: prerequisites come before the decisions that depend on them, and ties are broken by settle order. Unresolved items use the same order. The result is deterministic, so re-exports of an unchanged tree produce identical output.
- **Guard against scout misreading.** Only the markup above keeps the Unresolved section from being read as decisions. No scout changes are made in this feature.

## Testing Decisions

- **What makes a good test.** Tests assert on external behaviour: the planned file list and the rendered markdown for a given decision tree. They do not assert on internal helpers or intermediate data structures.
- **Pure renderer unit tests** in the style of the existing spec and ticket renderer tests. Each test builds a small decision tree and asserts on the output. Cases to cover:
  - A settled interviewer decision whose recommendation was accepted gets the "interviewer · accepted recommendation" label and no citation.
  - A user-introduced decision and an own-answer decision get the correct labels.
  - A repo decision the user reopened gets the reopened label, its original citation, and a "Supersedes" line quoting the original statement.
  - A kept repo decision appears only as a key-and-citation reference, with no restated statement.
  - A dropped repo decision does not appear anywhere.
  - Each non-settled state lands in Unresolved as "title — state", with no anchor, under the fixed heading and note.
  - Dependencies render as links to existing anchors.
  - Ordering is topological, with ties broken by settle order, and repeated renders produce byte-identical output.
  - The fallback label (introducer only) is used when the answer kind is absent.
- **Export plan tests.**
  - decisions.md is planned when at least one full entry exists.
  - It is not planned when there are only Unresolved items, only kept-repo references, or nothing at all.
- **Bundle-level tests** through the existing preview and export-session paths:
  - decisions.md shows in the preview.
  - It is written and listed in the manifest.
  - A re-export whose plan no longer includes it removes the previously written copy and nothing else.
- **Prior art.** The existing tests for the spec and ticket renderers, the export planning tests, and the preview-export and export-session bundle tests.

## Out of Scope

- Exporting intent.md.
- Adding provenance to the other exported files (spec, tickets, handoff, briefs).
- The manifest hash guard.
- Any change to the project scout. That includes a scout-side rule that ignores the Unresolved section, and carrying Unresolved items into the next session as open questions.
- Editing, annotating or flagging the original source file of a reopened repo decision.
- Session-and-round citations for user or interviewer decisions.
- Exporting rejected alternatives or the full question text.

## Further Notes

- The "how it was answered" label depends on the answer kind being persisted for every settled decision. The session state tells the kinds apart, which suggests they are stored, but the build must confirm this. If the kind is not persisted, persisting it becomes part of this work. If that is not feasible, fall back to showing the introducer alone.
- The Unresolved guard relies on the next scout honouring the markup. A follow-up ticket should consider a scout-side rule that skips the Unresolved section, or treats those items as open questions to carry forward.
- The design relies on the recorded loop: an exported decisions.md is found by the next scout as recorded decisions. That repo decision was dropped as a binding constraint for this session, but it still motivates how duplicates, supersession and Unresolved items are handled.

tickets.title: Make each settled decision's answer kind available to export
tickets.body:
## What to build

The decisions.md origin label needs to know how each settled decision was answered: accepted recommendation, chose another option, own answer, or repo-established.

- Confirm whether the answer kind is persisted with every settled decision, including decisions whose answer was replaced after a reopen.
- Confirm that it is exposed on the resolved decision view that export consumes.
- If the kind is only transient, persist it with the answer and expose it on the resolved view, keeping existing sessions readable. For older sessions with no stored kind, the kind is simply absent.
- If persisting it is not feasible, record that finding in the ticket so the renderer ships with the introducer-only fallback.

## How it is judged

- A settled decision's resolved view reports its answer kind for each kind the app produces.
- Sessions saved before this change still load, with the kind absent.
- Tests cover the round trip from answering to the resolved view.
- There are no changes to export output in this ticket.

tickets.title: Pure decisions.md renderer: full entries, origin labels, citations, ordering
tickets.body:
## What to build

Add a pure renderer next to the existing spec and ticket renderers. It takes the session's resolved decision tree and returns the text of decisions.md, with no filesystem access.

**Which decisions become full entries**
- Every settled decision introduced by the interviewer or the user.
- Every repo decision the interview reopened.

**What each full entry contains**
- A heading anchored by the stable decision key.
- A labelled field list: title, answer, reasoning, origin and citation.
- Dependencies rendered as links to the other entries' anchors.
- Nothing else: no question text and no rejected choices.

**Origin label**
- The introducer (interviewer, user or repo; repo adds recorded or inferred), plus how the answer was reached.
- The answer kind is mapped to plain phrases: "accepted recommendation", "chose another option", "own answer".
- When the answer kind is absent, fall back to the introducer alone.

**Citation**
- Repo-origin entries carry their original file-and-line citation.
- User and interviewer entries have no citation, and none is invented.

**Ordering**
- Topological: prerequisites before the decisions that depend on them, ties broken by settle order.
- Deterministic, so identical input gives byte-identical output.

This ticket does not cover reopened-repo supersession, kept-repo references or the Unresolved section (tickets 3 and 4). It also does not wire the renderer into the export plan (ticket 5).

## How it is judged

Unit tests in the style of the existing renderer tests, asserting only on the rendered markdown:
- An interviewer decision with an accepted recommendation gets the "interviewer · accepted recommendation" label and no citation.
- User-introduced, own-answer and chose-another-option decisions get the correct labels.
- The introducer-only fallback is used when the answer kind is absent.
- Dependency links point to existing anchors.
- Order is topological with the settle-order tiebreak.
- Repeated renders are byte-identical.

tickets.title: Render reopened repo decisions with Supersedes, and kept repo decisions as bare references
tickets.body:
## What to build

Extend the decisions.md renderer to cover repo-origin decisions.

**Reopened repo decisions** become full entries with:
- the new answer and its reasoning;
- the origin "repo (recorded) · reopened" or "repo (inferred) · reopened";
- a citation to the original source;
- a "Supersedes" line quoting the original repo statement.

The original source file is never read or written by export.

**Kept repo decisions** (settled, unchanged) are listed only as bare references: key and citation, with no restated statement and no anchor that marks them as entries.

**Dropped repo decisions** do not appear anywhere in the file.

References follow the same deterministic ordering as full entries.

## How it is judged

Unit tests on the rendered output:
- A reopened recorded decision and a reopened inferred decision each show the correct label, the citation and a Supersedes line quoting the original statement.
- A kept repo decision appears only as key plus citation, and its statement text is absent.
- A dropped repo decision's key, title and statement are absent from the output.
- Output stays byte-identical across repeated renders.

tickets.title: Render the Unresolved (not decisions) section
tickets.body:
## What to build

Extend the decisions.md renderer with an Unresolved section placed after all full entries and references.

**Section markup**
- A fixed heading, "Unresolved (not decisions)".
- A one-line note saying these are open questions and not decisions.

**Items**
- Each item is a plain list item, "title — state", with no key anchor and no link target.
- The section covers every non-settled decision: open, unasked, blocked, stale, deferred, unknown and prototype-flagged.
- Dropped repo decisions are excluded.
- Items appear in the same deterministic tree order as the entries.
- The section is omitted when there are no unresolved items.

## How it is judged

Unit tests on the rendered output:
- Each non-settled state appears as "title — state" under the fixed heading and note.
- The section comes after all entries.
- No Unresolved item has an anchor.
- Dropped repo decisions are excluded.
- There is no section when nothing is unresolved.
- Output is deterministic across repeated renders.

tickets.title: Wire decisions.md into the export plan, preview, write and manifest
tickets.body:
## What to build

Make the export planning step include decisions.md at the bundle root, beside the spec, when the session has at least one full entry. A full entry is a settled interviewer or user decision, or a reopened repo decision.

Do not plan the file when the session has any of the following and nothing else:
- only Unresolved items;
- only kept-repo references;
- nothing at all.

The bundle layer's preview, write, manifest and removal logic must handle decisions.md generically, with no special cases. A re-export whose plan no longer includes decisions.md removes a copy an earlier export wrote, and nothing else.

## How it is judged

**Export plan tests**
- The file is planned when a full entry exists.
- It is not planned in each of the empty cases above.

**Bundle-level tests** through the existing preview and export-session paths:
- decisions.md shows in the preview with the rendered content.
- It is written and listed in the manifest.
- A later re-export that no longer plans it removes only that file.
- The existing spec, ticket, handoff and brief outputs are unchanged.
